children: In the Phase 2 PURPOSE 5 trial, 52-week persistence was higher with twice-yearly lenacapavir than daily F/TDF. No HIV acquisitions occurred in the lenacapavir group; one occurred in the F/TDF group, where drug levels indicated fewer than two doses per week.
Zero HIV acquisitions with lenacapavir at Week 52
Supports the prevention profile, though the trial was designed to assess persistence and the release provides no statistical comparison for HIV acquisitions.
One HIV acquisition with F/TDF at Week 52
Drug-level analysis was consistent with fewer than two F/TDF doses per week, linking the event to low adherence rather than a direct efficacy comparison.
Retention was higher with lenacapavir; the release gives no prior-period comparison.
Rates were similar between groups; investigators found none related to study treatment.

This is an ongoing Phase 2 study adding persistence evidence to Gilead's lenacapavir HIV prevention program, rather than a new regulatory or commercial milestone. Further trial results or regulatory updates on lenacapavir for PrEP would be needed to establish a larger catalyst.
Based on the original press release from Gilead Sciences, Inc. distributed by BusinessWire.
